title: Mbappé Scores Twice. France Demolish Sweden 3-0 and He's Now One Goal From Messi's All-Time Record.
excerpt: The French captain's double at MetLife Stadium lifts his World Cup tally to 18 — one behind Lionel Messi — as Les Bleus set up a Round of 16 clash with Paraguay in Philadelphia.
body:
Kylian Mbappé doesn't chase records. Records chase him. And on a sweltering Tuesday evening at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — with 80,000 fans packed into the stands and the temperature pushing 32°C — the Frenchman made the kind of statement that renders debate irrelevant.

France 3, Sweden 0. Two of those goals belong to Mbappé. His World Cup tally now stands at 18 — just one behind Lionel Messi's all-time record of 19. He has done this in 18 matches. Messi needed 26.

The scoreline was generous to Sweden. France could have had six, maybe seven, were it not for Jacob Widell Zetterström pulling off save after acrobatic save in the Swedish goal. Les Bleus had 25 shots — 13 on target — to Sweden's seven. Possession was 61-39 in France's favour. This wasn't a contest. It was a coronation.

## The First Half: Patience, Then the Kill

For 44 minutes, Sweden held firm. Their compact defensive block kept France at bay, or so it seemed. But behind the lines, the pressure was relentless — Ousmane Dembélé probing on the right, Michael Olise threading passes through gaps that shouldn't have existed, and Mbappé lurking on the left, always a step away from detonation.

It came just before halftime. Olise and Dembélé combined for a short corner. The ball found Mbappé, who did a pair of stepovers, dropped his shoulder, left Viktor Gyökeres — the man who scored 36 goals for Sporting CP last season — sitting on the turf, and fired into the far post with a shot that carried more contempt than celebration.

That was his ninth knockout-stage goal in World Cup history. No one has ever scored more.

## The Second Half: Three Became an Avalanche



> **"His World Cup tally now stands at 18 — just one behind Lionel Messi's all-time record of 19."**


Eight minutes into the second half, Olise found his passing gear again. A through ball threaded between Gustaf Lagerbielke's legs found Bradley Barcola, who slotted into the top corner without breaking stride. Two-nil. Sweden were drowning.

Mbappé sealed it in the 74th minute. Another Olise assist — his fifth of the tournament, level at the top of the charts — another perfectly weighted reverse pass, another Mbappé finish curled beyond the goalkeeper. Eighteen goals. One away from Messi. Three World Cups, each one adding another chapter to an increasingly absurd résumé.

By the final whistle, France had become the first team to score three or more goals in five consecutive World Cup matches. That is not a team. That is a machine built to score.


![Lionel Messi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c8/Lionel_Messi_NE_Revolution_Inter_Miami_7.9.25-178_%28cropped_2%29.jpg)


## The Record Watch

The numbers are staggering. Mbappé's 18 goals have come across three World Cups: four in Russia 2018 (at age 19), eight in Qatar 2022, and six so far in this tournament. His 10 knockout-stage goals are an all-time record. He is 27 years old.

Messi's 19 goals came across five World Cups between 2006 and 2022 — the last of which, of course, produced that extraordinary final in Lusail where Mbappé scored a hat-trick in a losing cause.

Paraguay stand between Mbappé and another chance at the record. They meet on July 4 in Philadelphia, and on this evidence, the only question is whether the record falls in the first half or the second.

## For Indian Fans in America: The Beautiful Game on Your Doorstep

For the hundreds of thousands of Indian-Americans in the New York-New Jersey metro area — one of the densest NRI corridors on the planet — this World Cup has brought a different kind of sporting spectacle to their doorstep. MetLife Stadium, where cricket has never set foot, hosted a masterclass from the world's most electrifying footballer.

Indian sports fans in the US have long straddled two worlds: the IPL on one screen, the Premier League on another, and now the World Cup in their own backyard. The tournament moves to Santa Clara tomorrow for USA vs Bosnia-Herzegovina at Levi's Stadium — the heart of Silicon Valley's Indian tech diaspora — with kickoff at 5 PM PT on FOX.

For a generation of NRIs raising children who will grow up watching both Virat Kohli and Kylian Mbappé, these are the sporting moments that shape identity. And Mbappé is making sure they won't forget this one.

## What's Next

France face Paraguay on Saturday, July 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia (5 PM ET / 2 PM PT on FOX). On the other side of the bracket, Norway — who beat Ivory Coast 2-1 earlier Tuesday — will play Brazil at MetLife Stadium on July 5.

The French machine rolls on. And Mbappé is one goal away from football immortality.

**Sources:** Reuters, NBC Sports, USA Today, FOX Sports, Sky Sports
